My first `vitest run` against the three named failing files caught a genuine mid-edit race (reactionHandler.test.ts referenced an undefined `SELF_PUBKEY_FOR_FORWARDING_TEST` fixture) that had already resolved itself 90 seconds later once the teammates finished their turn. Distinguishing 'real stale-test bug' from 'I sampled mid-edit' required diff'ing file mtimes against my run timestamps and re-running the full suite three times consecutively before treating the tree as stable, rather than fixing what would have been someone else's in-flight edit out from under them.
retrospective.surprised_by: The task briefing flagged profileHandler.ts's own-join detection (`rumor.pubkey === authorPubkey` -> `sender.pubkey === authorPubkey`) as the most likely real regression. On inspection it is not: S1's dispatcher already drops any rumor where `rumor.pubkey !== sender.pubkey` before any handler runs, so the two are always equal in production, and every AC-PROD-4/AC-MARKER-6 relay-on-behalf test in the diff calls `makeSender(rumor.pubkey)` (sender mirrors rumor.pubkey), so the swap is a semantic no-op there and exactly the mandated attribution repointing, not an over-swap. The one path where sender.pubkey really can diverge from rumor.pubkey in this handler (the unsigned/legacy payloadToMemberProfile fallback) is the one S2 was explicitly told to swap, and it has a dedicated AC-ATTR-6 test with a forged sender. The signed-path own-join branch has no test exercising sender-divergence-while-signed (flagged as VQ-S2-008, post-impl) but that combination is unreachable in production today for the same dispatcher-guarantee reason.
